title: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling
description: Understand scaling strategies, load balancing, auto-scaling configurations, and when to scale horizontally vs vertically.

data.text: Vertical scaling adds resources to a single machine. Horizontal scaling adds more machines. Horizontal scaling provides better fault tolerance and unlimited scaling potential.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Vertical scaling: simpler but limited, good for databases
Horizontal scaling: more complex but unlimited, good for stateless services
Load balancers distribute traffic across instances
Auto-scale based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics
Stateful services require careful design for horizontal scaling
data.takeaway: Horizontal scaling is preferred for modern cloud applications due to fault tolerance and unlimited scale. Vertical scaling is still useful for databases and stateful components.
